Introduction

Starting a Home Care Agency in Oklahoma allows you to provide non-medical personal care services. The OK State Department of Health — Medical Facilities Service, Home Services Division oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Oklahoma’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Oklahoma’s Regulations

OSDH licenses home care agencies under Oklahoma Administrative Code. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the OK Secretary of State, apply for home care agency license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Oklahoma benchmarks: Private pay rates $18-$25/hour, Medicaid rates $14-$20/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Oklahoma requires background checks and training for all direct care staff.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting OSDH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Oklahoma City, Tulsa, and surrounding communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
